title.description: Title of the video or episode. Example: "Why sleep is a skill".

music.description: Background music. "auto" picks a fitting bundled track, "none" for silence, or a track id. Default "auto".

variety.description: How much the look varies from scene to scene inside the theme: "low", "medium" (default) or "high".

seed.description: Look seed. The same storyboard and seed always give the same video; a new seed gives a different cut. Omit to derive one from the title.

series.description: Series name. Videos in one series share a look family (the same seed unless a seed is given) so they read as one show, and the look stays locked against Shuffle.

reduceMotion.description: Calmer output: no camera moves and gentler entrances. Default false.

sfx.description: Sound effects (a whoosh on transitions, a tick on list items, a pop on emphasis) at a low level under the narration. "auto" (default) adds them, "off" leaves them out.

stings.description: A short chime at the start and another at the end of the video. "auto" adds them; omit for none.

sources.description: Pages you used for facts. Leave out if you used none. Never invent sources.

title.description: Title of the page or document. Example: "WHO sleep guidance".

url.description: Public http(s) address of the source.

accessed.description: Date you read it, YYYY-MM-DD. Example: "2026-11-13".

title.description: Title for posting, at most 100 characters. A clear promise, not clickbait. Example: "Why the sky is blue".

description.description: Post description: one or two sentences of what the viewer gets. No hashtags here; they go in hashtags.

hashtags.description: Up to ten hashtags, with or without the # sign.

thumbnailText.description: Three to six big words for the thumbnail, at most 40 characters. Example: "Why is the sky blue?".

publish.description: How to post the video: title, description, hashtags and thumbnail text. Leave out what you are unsure of.

language.description: The language the narration is written in, when it is not American English: "en-GB", "es", "fr", "hi", "it", "ja", "pt-BR" or "zh". The voice is chosen to match.

format.description: Canvas shape. "9:16" vertical for Reels, Shorts and TikTok; "16:9" landscape for YouTube; "1:1" square. Default "9:16".

theme.description: Optional visual theme: "bold-pop", "clean-minimal", "midnight-tech", "editorial-paper", "neon", "warm-documentary", "corporate-blue", "playful-pastel", "mono-brutalist" or "cinematic". Omit or use "auto" to let Reel Studio choose a theme that fits the content.

enabled.description: Narrate the video with a local voice. Default true.

voiceId.description: Voice name from the voice list, for example "af_heart". Omit to use the default voice.

speed.description: Speaking speed, 0.7 to 1.3. Omit for natural speed (1.0).

style.description: How the voice reads: "calm", "energetic", "storyteller" or "news". Omit for the natural read.

voice.description: Narration settings. Omit to narrate with the default voice.

captions.description: Captions generated from the narration. "auto" shows them, "off" hides them. Default "auto".

chapters.description: Long videos only (over about three minutes): where each chapter starts, so the description gets timestamps. Leave out for short videos.

title.description: Chapter title, at most 60 characters. Example: "How light scatters".

startScene.description: Number of the scene where this chapter starts, counting from 0. The first chapter starts at 0. Start each chapter with a scene that names it.

type.description: What the scene is. hook: opening line that grabs attention. statement: one key idea. kinetic-text: a punchy line slammed word by word. list: 2-6 short points (needs items). steps: 2-6 numbered steps in order (needs items). checklist: 2-6 things to tick off (needs items). stat: one big number (needs stat). comparison: two options side by side (needs compare). before-after: a change from one state to another (needs compare). timeline: 2-5 moments in order (needs points). diagram: 2-5 connected parts of a process or system (needs points). chart: compare values (needs chart; chart.kind bar, line or donut). quote: a quotation (needs quote). definition: a term and its meaning (needs definition). code: a code snippet (needs code). terminal: shell commands and output (needs code). media: a full-frame picture or clip (needs media). media-split: picture beside the headline (needs media). device-mockup: a phone screen showing a picture (media optional). cta: closing call to action. Example: "statement".

headline.description: Short on-screen text, at most 60 characters, a complete phrase that is not cut off. Example: "Sleep is a skill".

narration.description: What the voice says: full sentences, at most 400 characters, written to be heard. Do not repeat the headline word for word. Example: "Most adults need seven to nine hours. Treat sleep like training, not an afterthought."

body.description: Optional supporting line shown under the headline, at most 200 characters.

items.description: Points for a list scene, 2 to 6. Example: ["Same bedtime", "No screens", "Cool room"].
One short point, at most 60 characters.

stat.description: Key number for a stat scene.

value.description: The big figure, at most 12 characters. Example: "73%".

label.description: What the figure measures, at most 40 characters. Example: "report better focus".

labels.description: Category labels along the axis. Example: ["2023", "2024", "2025"].

label.description: Name of this data series. Example: "Users".

values.description: One number per label, in the same order. Use real figures only.

unit.description: Unit shown with the numbers, for example "%" or "k".

series.description: One to three data series. Each needs one value per label.

source.description: Where the numbers come from. Example: "Company report, 2025".

kind.description: How to draw it: "bar" to compare, "line" for change over time, "donut" for shares of a whole (first series only). Default "bar".

chart.description: Data for a chart scene. Never invent numbers.

compare.description: Two sides for a comparison or before-after scene: left is the first option or the before state.

label.description: Short title of this side. Example: "Before".

text.description: One short sentence about this side, at most 80 characters.

left.description: The first option, or the before state. Example: {"label":"Before","text":"One hour per edit"}.

label.description: Short title of this side. Example: "Before".

text.description: One short sentence about this side, at most 80 characters.

right.description: The second option, or the after state. Example: {"label":"After","text":"One minute"}.

points.description: Two to five moments (timeline) or parts (diagram), in order. Example: [{"label":"2019","text":"Launch"},{"label":"2024","text":"1M users"}].

label.description: A date, name or step title. Example: "2024".

text.description: Optional short detail, at most 70 characters.

definition.description: Term and meaning for a definition scene.

quote.description: Quotation for a quote scene. Only real, attributed quotes.

text.description: The quotation, at most 160 characters, exactly as said.

attribution.description: Who said it. Example: "Dr. Mara Lin, sleep researcher".

text.description: The snippet, at most 12 lines and 600 characters.

query.description: Plain-words search for a fitting stock picture or clip. Example: "sunrise over a quiet city street".

assetId.description: Id of an asset already in the project's library.

generate.description: Describe a picture to make with a local image model, in plain words. Only used when the person has set one up; otherwise "query" (or the headline) finds a stock picture instead. Example: "a lighthouse on a cliff at dusk, calm sea".

path.description: Relative path of a supplied file. Example: "media/demo.mp4".

media.description: Picture or clip for the scene. Provide exactly one of query, assetId, path or generate (generate may also carry a query as its fallback).

icon.description: Optional icon name in lowercase words joined by hyphens. Example: "moon".

illustration.description: Optional looping background illustration: one of sixty names such as "stars-2" or "bars-1", a motif ("orbits", "waves", "bubbles", "network", "bars", "rays", "leaves", "skyline", "gears", "dots", "stars", "spiral") or a related word like "space" or "growth". Decorative only.

emphasis.description: Up to three words from the headline or body to highlight. Example: ["skill"].

items.description: A word or short phrase copied from the headline or body.

pace.description: How fast this scene is read: "slow" for a key idea or a number that should land, "fast" for a quick aside. Omit for the normal pace.

durationHint.description: Rough seconds for the scene, 2 to 30. Only a hint: real timing follows the narration length. Omit unless you need a longer pause.

items.description: One scene: what is shown and what is said.

scenes.description: Scenes in order. About 8 scenes make a 60-second video; a long video can use up to 120. Start with a hook and end with a cta or a statement that closes the idea.

title.description: Title of the video or episode. Example: "Why sleep is a skill".

music.description: Background music. "auto" picks a fitting bundled track, "none" for silence, or a track id. Default "auto".

variety.description: How much the look varies from scene to scene inside the theme: "low", "medium" (default) or "high".

seed.description: Look seed. The same storyboard and seed always give the same video; a new seed gives a different cut. Omit to derive one from the title.

series.description: Series name. Videos in one series share a look family (the same seed unless a seed is given) so they read as one show, and the look stays locked against Shuffle.

sources.description: Pages you used for facts. Leave out if you used none. Never invent sources.

title.description: Title of the page or document. Example: "WHO sleep guidance".

url.description: Public http(s) address of the source.

accessed.description: Date you read it, YYYY-MM-DD. Example: "2026-11-13".

title.description: Title for posting, at most 100 characters. A clear promise, not clickbait. Example: "Why the sky is blue".

description.description: Post description: one or two sentences of what the viewer gets. No hashtags here; they go in hashtags.

hashtags.description: Up to ten hashtags, with or without the # sign.

thumbnailText.description: Three to six big words for the thumbnail, at most 40 characters. Example: "Why is the sky blue?".

publish.description: How to post the video: title, description, hashtags and thumbnail text. Leave out what you are unsure of.

language.description: The language the narration is written in, when it is not American English: "en-GB", "es", "fr", "hi", "it", "ja", "pt-BR" or "zh". The voice is chosen to match.

id.description: Short id used by turns. Example: "host".

voiceId.description: Voice name. Omit for the default voice.

speakers.description: One to three speakers: solo narration, a two-host talk or an interview.

speaker.description: The id of a speaker listed in speakers.

text.description: What this speaker says, at most 600 characters, written to be heard.

anyOf.description: A podcast storyboard: speakers and their turns.
